name: Explainability

subjectOf.text: The black box character of deep learning models is a governance failure and not merely a technical inconvenience: opacity obstructs debugging, obscures bias detection and mitigation, and prevents comprehension of how inputs become outputs.
subjectOf.abstract: This opacity can obstruct the debugging process, obscure bias detection and mitigation, and hinder comprehension of AI decision-making.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI Governance (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4796714
scope_conditions: most pronounced in deep learning models
matters where decisions must be explained or audited

subjectOf.text: The opacity of deep learning models obstructs debugging, obscures the detection and mitigation of bias, and prevents comprehension of how AI decisions are reached.
subjectOf.abstract: This opacity can obstruct the debugging process, obscure bias detection and mitigation, and hinder comprehension of AI decision-making.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI Governance Via Web3 Reputation System (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4941807
scope_conditions: particularly in deep learning models whose internal decision mechanisms are not transparent

subjectOf.text: Concrete cases show the cost of AI opacity: Nvidia self driving cars that learn from human behavior might confuse the moon for a traffic light, and the DeepPatient project predicted disease onset accurately from medical records while offering no explanation for its predictions.
subjectOf.abstract: For example, Nvidia's self-driving cars learn from human behavior but might confuse the moon for a traffic light, and the DeepPatient project accurately predicted disease onset from medical records without providing explanations for its predictions
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI Governance Via Web3 Reputation System (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4941807
scope_conditions: in deep learning systems deployed in driving and medical prediction

subjectOf.text: Legal and ethical challenges intensify when AI is deployed in critical decision making roles that significantly affect human lives and the reasoning behind the AI decision is opaque.
subjectOf.abstract: Legal and ethical challenges are heightened when AI is deployed in critical decision-making roles that significantly impact human lives, particularly when the reasoning behind AI's decisions is opaque.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI Governance Via Web3 Reputation System (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4941807
scope_conditions: in determinative decisions such as parole eligibility, employment, and medical strategy
where the reasoning behind the decision is not visible

subjectOf.text: The distinctive strength of case-based reasoning systems, exemplified by HYPO, is that they model legal argumentation in a detailed and realistic manner rather than merely producing an outcome.
subjectOf.abstract: A clear strength of the HYPO program was to model legal argumentation in a detailed and realistic manner. This reflects the strength of case-based reasoning systems.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Morgan A. Gray, The Evolving Role of Artificial Intelligence in Law (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5541658
scope_conditions: case-based reasoning systems that compare a problem case with precedent cases

subjectOf.text: Accuracy alone is insufficient for legal AI: a model must also be explainable before its outputs can be trusted in judicial settings.
subjectOf.abstract: Accuracy alone is insufficient without explainability.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Morgan A. Gray, The Evolving Role of Artificial Intelligence in Law (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5541658
scope_conditions: predictive AI used in legal and judicial applications
